name: NVIDIA NVLink 6.0
bandwidth_basis: PER LINK, UNIDIRECTIONAL. NVIDIA's official NVLink product page spec table (link-nvlink-switch-spec, accessed 2026-10-03) confirms 3,000 GB/s per GPU and 36 max links per GPU for Sixth Generation NVLink: 3000 / 36 = 83.3 GB/s per link bidirectional, so 41.7 GB/s per link per direction - the recorded value. NVIDIA marks the table preliminary. A secondary source (Wikipedia) states 3.6 TB/s bidirectional per GPU, but this figure does not appear in any first-party NVIDIA document and is not supported by NVIDIA's own spec page.
topology: Direct GPU-to-GPU links plus switch fabric; Vera Rubin NVL72 connects 72 GPUs all-to-all as one non-blocking compute fabric.
switching: NVLink 6 Switch spans 8-GPU and 72-GPU domains. NVIDIA states the NVL72 rack interconnects every GPU pair at 3 TB/s and adds SHARP in-network reduction, plus control-plane resilience and hot-swappable switch trays.
notes: Vera Rubin generation. NVIDIA's official NVLink product page spec table (accessed 2026-10-03) confirms 3,000 GB/s per GPU and 36 max links per GPU for Sixth Generation NVLink, marked preliminary. The 3,600 GB/s figure from Wikipedia (link-wikipedia-nvlink) has no first-party NVIDIA support and is not used. Internal consistency check: 72 GPUs x 3 TB/s = 216 TB/s matches the NVL72 rack total. NVIDIA's 1.7x claim vs previous generation is consistent with 3000/1800 = 1.67. Inference consequence: tensor-parallel sharding wants the highest per-direction fabric rate available, because every layer boundary ships activations across the link. The bidirectional aggregate figure that dominates marketing is not what a single collective move sees.
